resultText: Found and fixed it. In `packages/element/src/mutateElement.ts:65-66`, the code used `updates.x || element.x` and `updates.y || element.y` to compute the arrow's position before recalculating its elbow route. Since `0` is falsy, moving the arrow to exactly `x = 0` or `y = 0` caused the fallback to kick in and silently reuse the old coordinate — the route (and thus final position) was recomputed relative to the stale origin, so the move appeared to do nothing. Any non-zero coordinate is truthy, so it always worked fine. Changed both to `??` so only `undefined`/`null` triggers the fallback, preserving `0` as a valid explicit value.

resultText:
## Root cause

In `packages/element/src/mutateElement.ts`, the elbow-arrow repositioning branch built the base point for recomputing the route with:

```ts
x: updates.x || element.x,
y: updates.y || element.y,
```

Since `0` is falsy, an explicit `updates.x = 0` (or `updates.y = 0`) was discarded in favor of the *old* `element.x`/`element.y`. The rerouted points/position that `updateElbowArrowPoints` computes (and which get spread back into `updates`, overwriting whatever `x`/`y` was originally passed) end up based on the stale coordinate — so the arrow silently keeps its old position whenever the target is exactly 0. Any non-zero target is truthy, so it was never nulled out and worked correctly.

## Fix

Changed to nullish coalescing so only `undefined` falls back, not `0`:

```ts
x: updates.x ?? element.x,
y: updates.y ?? element.y,
```

`packages/element/src/mutateElement.ts:65-66`

I also added a regression test at `packages/element/tests/reproMove.test.tsx` that mutates an elbow arrow to `x: 0, y: 0` alongside `points` (the same call shape used by resizing/rerouting code) and asserts the coordinates actually land on `0`.

**Note:** I don't have shell/Bash access in this session, so I could not run `yarn test:update` or `yarn test:typecheck` to confirm the test passes — please run those before committing.

**Root cause:** in `mutateElement.ts`, before recomputing elbow arrow routing, the code built the position to route from via `updates.x || element.x`. `0` is falsy, so moving to `x = 0` (or `y = 0`) silently discarded the new coordinate and reused the old one — the arrow's routing was computed as if it hadn't moved. Fixed by switching to `??`, which only falls back on `undefined`/`null`, not `0`.
